memory_update.text: SPSC is the strongest underfollowed candidate for the node because it maps directly to retailer-supplier product/item data validation, assortment, fulfillment, and inventory analytics rather than generic ecommerce software.

SMWB is a speculative small-cap digital shelf analytics candidate; inclusion depends on proving Retail Intelligence is material and tied to AI-mediated product discovery rather than just a product-label refresh.

YEXT is a speculative AI-search visibility and structured brand-data candidate; later layers should test whether Scout creates durable ARR reacceleration or remains a competitive feature in legacy local SEO/listings.

Retail-media measurement and data clean rooms are adjacent chokepoints to product discovery because retailer algorithms and AI agents need sales, audience, attribution, and product-level feedback loops.

Private companies dominate many pure-play product-content and digital-shelf categories, including ratings/reviews, PIM, marketplace optimization, and feed management; public-market exposure may be indirect or embedded in broader software/data companies.

node: AI-mediated shopping, retail data and product-content infrastructure
summary: Expanded the universe around AI-mediated retail discovery and product-content/data infrastructure with a two-lane funnel. Reference/context exposure is represented by LiveRamp as a scaled retail-media/data-collaboration platform. The underfollowed discovery lane centers on SPS Commerce, Similarweb, and Yext: all are US-listed, mostly small/mid-cap, and map to less obvious chokepoints in product data exchange, digital shelf analytics, AI-search visibility, reviews/listings, inventory or retail-media measurement. Key caveat: this node remains early; later layers must prove that AI shopping, retail media, and marketplace ranking changes are creating incremental durable revenue rather than merely improving narrative fit.
